slides.headline: AI COMPANIES GOT CAUGHT PIRATING BOOKS. NOW THEY BUY THEM — AND FEED THEM TO A BLADE
ANTHROPIC RAN MILLIONS OF BOOKS THROUGH A HYDRAULIC BLADE
slides.body: The company behind Claude bought used books by the truckload, chopped the spines off with a hydraulic cutter, scanned every page — then threw the pages away. It's faster and cheaper than scanning a book without destroying it. And they did it on purpose, at industrial scale

slides.headline: SOUNDS ILLEGAL. A JUDGE SAID IT'S NOT
slides.body: Once you buy a book, it's yours — an old rule called first-sale doctrine. A judge ruled scanning your own books is fair use. The $1.5 billion Anthropic just paid authors? That was for pirating e-books. So the industry switched: buy the real thing, destroy it legally

slides.headline: ONE SELLER SHIPS UP TO 1,000,000 BOOKS PER ORDER — AND HIDES WHO'S BUYING
slides.body: A quiet book database called ISBNdb now bulk-sells AI companies 1,000 to 1 million books at a time — and promises to keep every buyer's name secret. The hottest items: books printed before 2022. They're the last writing on Earth guaranteed to be human, made before AI junk flooded the internet

slides.headline: THEY'RE SPENDING MILLIONS ON SOMETHING YOUR BUSINESS ALREADY OWNS
slides.body: All of this is a hunt for one thing: real human writing AI hasn't touched. Your business is sitting on years of it — emails, customer calls, notes, the way you actually do things. That's exactly the fuel an AI needs to take over half your daily busywork — no new hires, no blade required
